title: Optimize edge-router chunking and stabilize function-call handshake in OpenAI compatibility layer
author: Jordan Park
commits: c1a4b7d: router: implement adaptive chunk heuristic based on downstream ack latency
8f9e2a1: proxy: add explicit function-call handshake and conservative backoff for tool streams
bb3d9f0: tests/docs: e2e test for fn-call streaming + docs and perf notes
changed_files: gateway/router/edge_router.go — adjust chunking heuristic and maxChunkBytes
gateway/proxy/stream_handshake.go — strengthen function-call negotiation and timeouts
compat/openai/route_map.go — add fallback rules to prefer local-model variant for tool-calls
docs/compatibility/openai-migration.md — migration notes for client buffer sizes and retry guidance
ci/pipelines/integration-perf.yml — mark streaming e2e as rerunnable to reduce flakes
third_party/benchmarks/edge_chunking/README.md — microbench results for different chunk sizes
description:
Context: customers and internal benchmarks showed intermittent stalls and increased tail latency for long-running function/tool call streams when the gateway proxied small fixed chunks to downstream model backends. The OpenAI compatibility layer also had ambiguous fallback behavior when a function call triggered a model variant routing (hosted vs dedicated), causing duplicate tool activations in edge cases.

Motivation: reduce tail latencies and prevent duplicate tool invocations while keeping OpenAI-compatible behaviour intact. This change tunes the edge routing/chunking heuristic to be workload-aware and makes the function-call handshake explicit so the proxy and model backend agree on stream framing and tool activation before payload streaming starts.

What I changed: consolidated in three places: router, proxy handshake, and compat route mapping. The edge router now measures downstream ACK latency (smoothed window) and picks a chunk size that balances throughput and per-chunk processing overhead. The proxy implements a lightweight function-call negotiation: a two-step preflight (call-intent + accept/reject) before streaming token chunks. Route mapping updates ensure tool-calls prefer a local-model fallback if the primary route would create a duplicate external tool activation.

Testing and validation: unit tests for the handshake state machine, e2e streaming test exercising deterministic chunk boundaries, microbenchmarks included in third_party, and manual smoke tests against hosted and dedicated environments. CI transient failures observed for e2e streaming were addressed by making the pipeline rerunnable.

Rollout: feature gated behind 'edge_router_adaptive_chunking' and 'fncall_explicit_handshake' feature flags; staged rollout to 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor token tail-latency and tool-invocation-dups metric, then 100% if green. Backport candidates: small changes to route_map and handshake are candidates for release/1.9.
review_conversation: Aisha Gupta requested changes: tighten timeouts on handshake and add metrics for handshake failures (added metric fncall.handshake.fail_count and updated tests)
Jordan Park replied: implemented timeout reduction to 250ms and exposed metrics, updated tests to assert metric increments
Marco Salazar comment: can we avoid changing default maxChunkBytes in hosted fleets? Answer: heuristic preserves current default until avg ACK latency crosses threshold, config override available
Evan Lee approval: Verified e2e in staging with 0.6x tail latency for long tool streams, approves merge
release_notes: Improves streaming stability and reduces tail latency for long function/tool streams by introducing adaptive chunking in the edge router and an explicit function-call handshake. Adds metrics to detect handshake failures and a compatibility route fallback to prevent duplicate external tool activations.
notes: Feature flags enabled by default in staging. Monitor fncall.handshake.* and router.chunking.avg_ack_latency; rollback plan included in the rollout docs. Consider backport to 1.9.x for urgent enterprise customers.
